provisional_claims.summary: Courier (field packets) defects: (1) precedes() iterated the wrong clock's keys so any event looked superseded by unrelated contexts; (2) _covered() pooled contexts from every record, so sharing one observation dropped other records' edits; (3) project() kept contexts for unselected records, so merging a selection erased notes it didn't include; (4) event contexts and checkpoint contexts used the packet-wide clock, so after receiving a projection a writer "saw" edits it never got and overwrote them / checkpoint dropped them; now per-record record_clock; (5) duplicate-dot check only compared record, not full event; (6) merged packet kept stale counter so continuing left writer reused dots; (7) concurrent edit+delete hid the observation (any False -> all False); (8) conflicting values deduplicated with casefold, losing exact case; (9) put/from_garden aliased caller-supplied values; (10) acknowledged() used max instead of min across named devices (missing ack must give 0); CLI reads UTF-8.
provisional_claims.reproduction: a=new_packet('A'); put(a,'r1',{'text':'one'}); b=merge(new_packet('B'),a); put(a,'r1',{'text':'Fern'}); put(b,'r1',{'text':'fern'}); observations(merge(a,b)) showed one value; remove(a,'r1') vs put(b,...) hid record; project(a,['r1']) merged into b then b edits r2 silently overwrote A's unseen r2 edit; acknowledged({'A':{'A':3},'B':{'A':2}},['A','B']) returned 3 instead of 2.

provisional_claims.reproduction: season(0) returned 'Highsummer'; calendar_day(0)['season_day']==2; glowcap lived to 105; shade_cloth at (x,y-1)... effective_shade(x,y) ignored cloth on tile below; almanac longest_dry_spell counted drizzle days; calendar showed plan run at day+repeat when remaining==1.

provisional_claims.summary: save_merge: _logical_id mapped every record (including records newly created on a replica) to ["base", id], so independently created notes/tasks/etc. with the same number on both devices collided and were merged/conflicted as if one record, and new records were never re-allocated fresh ids. Now non-ancestor ids are namespaced by replica origin and get unique allocations recorded in the receipt. Also reject a supplied "ancestor" that is newer (later day) than a replica.
provisional_claims.reproduction: b=create(3,6,6); add_note(b,'base'); l,r=deepcopy(b),deepcopy(b); add_note(l,'left new'); add_note(r,'right new'); reconcile(b.to_dict(),l.to_dict(),r.to_dict(),left_origin='desk',right_origin='field') -> previously a conflict on /records/notes/["base",2]/text instead of ready with both notes (ids 3,4).

provisional_claims.summary: Campaign/runtime defects: (1) runtime.execution_version ignored the campaign's recorded release and always ran conservation-2; now uses definition["runtime"]["id"]. (2) CampaignStore.publish fencing accepted stale workers ("generation = ? OR owner != ?") — now requires matching generation AND owner. (3) publish committed branch state before inserting its checkpoint/report in a separate transaction (non-atomic progress); now one transaction. (4) fork re-applied events at the checkpoint offset even though that care is already in the checkpoint garden (offset <= → offset <). (5) compact computed protected descendant-origin checkpoints but deleted them anyway; now retained. Also habitat.water_balance: rain barrels added 6 moisture every day instead of only rainy days (classic-1 contract).
provisional_claims.reproduction: Create campaign with --version classic-1 and rain_barrel: results matched conservation-2. Two claims of same branch after lease expiry: stale worker's publish was accepted. Fork a branch at offset 4 of 'Extra water' treatment: water at offset 4 applied twice. Fork from offset 6 then compact --every 5: provenance of child failed 'Checkpoint is unavailable'. Barrel tile on a clear day gained +6 moisture.

provisional_claims.summary: field_calibration.estimate: least-squares spread/covariance were computed on raw timestamps (sum t^2 - (sum t)^2/n), catastrophically cancelling for realistic epoch/fractional timestamps (e.g. 1.7e9 s) and giving wrong trends; duplicate timestamps were not averaged before fitting as documented; non-numeric/bool readings were silently coerced. Now fit uses centered offsets, averages shared timestamps, validates numeric readings. calibrated_sources keeps ponds at 100 / stones at 0.
provisional_claims.reproduction: estimate([{'timestamp':1.7e9+0.25,'moisture':42},{'timestamp':1.7e9+60.25,'moisture':44},{'timestamp':1.7e9+120.25,'moisture':43}], 1.7e9+120.25) should equal the same readings at 0/60/120 (43.5) but differed; readings sharing a timestamp were weighted by count instead of averaged.

provisional_claims.summary: History defects: (1) replay checkpoint cache key hashed only the last event (events[-1:]), so different histories sharing a final event reused the wrong cached garden; key now covers the whole prefix. (2) _resolved_command replayed the authoring-time numeric binding instead of the logical reference's current local ID, so corrections that renumber objects made later edits hit the wrong/missing object. (3) cherry-pick identity used command content, so independently authored identical actions were deduplicated; identity is now the event ID. (4) rebase order check only honoured the target's order, ignoring contradictory local orders; now checks both. (5) rebase used the parent's current head instead of the fork's recorded base_revision. (6) correct resolved numeric IDs in replacements against the final garden instead of the garden at that point in the (corrected) history.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create; append note A; append note B; append edit_note ident=<B's id>; correct {A_event: null} -> previously conflicted (edit targeted old numeric ID); now B edited with its new ID. Fork, append to parent and fork, rebase fork onto parent after parent advanced: used parent's current head as base -> wrong merge. Append identical water command to two branches, cherry-pick one: previously dropped as duplicate.

provisional_claims.summary: Irrigation: (1) irrigation_flow.allocate's augmenting-path search skipped residual reverse arcs (edge.pipe is None), so it was a greedy flow that could deliver less than supply/capacities permit (not maximum flow); (2) irrigation.solve pruned candidate schedules by an aggregate census signature, so different gardens with identical census averages were merged and the truly best schedule could be discarded; states are now deduplicated only on the full world + remaining water + offset. load_design also checks the replayed remaining water.
provisional_claims.reproduction: allocate([{'from':'tank','to':'a','capacity':1},{'from':'tank','to':'b','capacity':1},{'from':'a','to':'b','capacity':1}],'tank',{'b':2,'a':1},5): first path tank->a->b consumes a, greedy then stops at total 1; max flow is 2 (tank->b, reverse a->b, a->sink).

provisional_claims.summary: workspace_catalog: upgrading a format-1 catalog ran REINDEX before installing the format-2 catalog_key function, so the label index stayed keyed by the old casefold-only normalizer while queries used NFKC/space-folded keys (stale index: searches for fullwidth/spaced labels miss, integrity errors). Now installs the new key then reindexes; unversioned catalogs with existing receipts are treated as format 1; key re-normalizes after casefold; import validates receipt shape and accepts format-1 items without locator.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Create a v1 catalog (catalog_format version 1, index on casefold key) containing label 'Ｆield  Pond'; open with WorkspaceCatalog and search('field pond') -> previously no match / PRAGMA integrity_check reported index mismatch; now found and integrity ok.

provisional_claims.summary: History exchange: _common_bases truncated the maximal common ancestors to one (maximal[:1]), so criss-cross reconciliations (both collaborators previously combined the same work) used an arbitrary single base and could drop/resurrect later edits or reversions; now returns all maximal common bases so comparison() merges them (or reports ambiguous-ancestry).
provisional_claims.reproduction: Two installations A,B share a channel; each publishes an edit, both reconcile the pair (two distinct merge publications), then A adds a note and B edits/reverts an earlier note and publishes; reconciling the two new heads picked only one of the two merge publications as base, so the edit/reversion from the other side's merge ancestry was mis-attributed.

provisional_claims.summary: Staged studies: (1) later stages seeded every treatment (and control) from the previous stage's *control* checkpoint, discarding the promoted treatment's earlier care/results; now each job continues from its own treatment's checkpoint. (2) Stage decision was taken as soon as any source had a complete control+candidates (support["common"]), so worker completion order decided promotion and the 'no eligible garden -> failed study' path never fired; decision now waits until all stage trials are terminal (complete or failed).
provisional_claims.reproduction: create examples/study.json with two stages; work to finish stage 0; stage-1 treatment job parent/anchor has treatment 'control' and its initial world lacks the treatment's stage-0 care. With two sources, finishing source A's jobs first finalized the stage report before source B's jobs ran (report excluded B although B later completed).

provisional_claims.summary: Ensembles: (1) ensemble_reports.summarize zipped controls.values() with the paired treatment rows, so when a control was missing/failed or order differed each treatment was compared against another garden's control; now pairs by replicate label; (2) ensemble_compute.evaluate returned the cached origin's identity on a cache hit, so two sources with equal saves were reported as the same replicate (b's trials labelled as a); identity is now always the requested replicate/treatment with provenance in cache_origin; (3) EnsembleStore.report recomputed the result from current outcomes instead of returning the published envelope, so old revisions' reports changed after edits/work; (4) publish validated only previously-known reads, so a fresh node computed from inputs edited concurrently was accepted with stale data; now also checks the computation's actual reads against current digests.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create an ensemble with sources {'a':S,'b':S} (equal saves), work to completion: outcomes for b carried identity replicate 'a' (cache hit). Edit a plan after revision 0 publishes then report(e,0) returned numbers from the new revision's outcomes. prepare() a fresh node, edit its source, then publish -> accepted stale result.

provisional_claims.summary: Reproducibility regressions verified against the shipped examples: (1) planning.run_plans kept a reference to the plan dict from before tend_many replaced world.workbench, so a successful care plan never decremented remaining/advanced its day (it re-ran/stalled; lantern-hollow plan stayed day 2, remaining 3 instead of day 8, remaining 1). Re-fetch the entry after tending. (2) commands.execute bumped revision by the inner function's increments +1 (a 16-command replay gave revision 37, grow days=5 added 6); a command is now exactly one revision (world.revision+1), matching examples/lantern-hollow.json revision 16. (3) engine: the daily +1 nutrient recovery was applied to planted tiles too (masking the hunger penalty when nutrients were just below upkeep), and the strained-plant nutrient return used the previous day's vitality; now only bare ground recovers and strain uses the day's vitality. create(34,16,11)+step(24) now reproduces examples/first-garden.json cells and journal exactly (was 17 differing cells, wrong glowcap count on day 21).
provisional_claims.reproduction: python3 -B -m mosslight new h.json --seed 34 && python3 -B -m mosslight replay h.json examples/hollow-actions.json; compare with examples/lantern-hollow.json (previously revision 37 vs 16, plan day/remaining wrong, cells moisture differ). create(34,16,11); step(w,24) vs examples/first-garden.json cells/journal (previously 17 cells differ, 'At dusk, 9 glowcap' vs 8).

provisional_claims.summary: engine._one_day: the "hungry soil" comfort penalty (-7 when nutrients below species upkeep) was tested against the tile's nutrients after the bare-ground +1 recovery, so plants on 1-nutrient soil (upkeep 2) escaped the penalty and starving plants kept too much vitality. Penalty now uses the start-of-day nutrients. With this fix create(34,16,11)+step(24) reproduces examples/first-garden.json exactly (cells and journal), and new --seed 34 + replay examples/hollow-actions.json reproduces examples/lantern-hollow.json exactly.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(34,16,11); step(w,24); compare with examples/first-garden.json: before the fix 17 cells differed (e.g. cell 3 moss vitality 100 vs 93, cell 15 nutrients 15 vs 16) and journal day 21 said 9 glowcaps instead of 8; after the fix 0 differences.

provisional_claims.summary: More core fixes: (1) World.to_dict returned journal entries shared with the live garden (list() shallow copy), and from_dict kept the caller's journal dicts, so editing a to_dict()/source save mutated the world — now entries are copied (PORTABILITY: to_dict is independently editable). (2) weather.next_weather searched from today (start=world.day) instead of the future (tomorrow onward). (3) harvest only subtracted 5 age days, so an old plant could be harvested repeatedly at once; harvesting now starts a new growth period (age 0) as documented. (4) World.index accepted booleans as coordinates (isinstance(True,int)); now strict integers. (5) field_calibration.estimate now fits in exact rational arithmetic, so large/fractional timestamps (e.g. 1e17 s offsets) no longer lose precision.

Plant age 30 moss harvested twice in a row succeeded. w.index(True,0) returned 1. estimate at 1e17+{0,60,120} differed from 0/60/120.

provisional_claims.summary: weather.next_weather searched an almanac starting today (start=world.day) although it must find a matching *future* day (almanac/next weather start tomorrow); now uses the default tomorrow start, so today's weather is never returned. analysis.transect used a strict `double > dy` Bresenham test, which breaks the standard line walk on exact half-step ties (e.g. (0,0)->(1,2) stepped straight to (0,1) before the diagonal, unlike the symmetric x-major case); now uses the standard `>=` test so lines through tile centers are consistent.

provisional_claims.summary: history_exchange reconciliation was operand-order dependent: _merge_events rebased left onto right, so two collaborators reconciling the same pair of heads (each naming its own publication first) produced merge publications with contradictory orders of the concurrent actions. The next round of independent work then failed with an "order-conflict" (or dropped/reordered later edits and reversions) even though nothing actually conflicted. The top-level merge now uses a canonical operand order (sorted publication ids, which every installation shares), so both sides of a criss-cross converge on identical event lists and later edits/reversions are retained.
provisional_claims.reproduction: A announces a 2-note history; B receives. A edits note 1 (pa), B edits note 2 (pb); exchange parcels. A: reconcile(pa,pb); B: reconcile(pb,pa) -> previously different event orders. A reverts note 1 and publishes, B adds note 3 and publishes; after exchange reconcile(pa2,pb2) raised HistoryConflict order-conflict. Now merged -> ['one','two-B','three'] identically on both installations, and a further round with B's reversion also merges.

provisional_claims.summary: History, history-exchange and study CLIs read and wrote JSON files with the platform default encoding (Path.read_text()/write_text() without encoding) while emitting ensure_ascii=False JSON, so non-ASCII notes/titles in exported gardens and parcels failed or were mis-decoded under non-UTF-8 locales; they now read/write UTF-8 explicitly (history fallback fingerprint source too).

provisional_claims.summary: history.HistoryStore.correct resolved numeric object IDs in a replacement command against the wrong garden (originally the final result; the loop's `index` was computed but unused). Numeric IDs in a replacement must refer to the garden at that point in the history being corrected, so the replacement is now canonicalized against a replay of the original events before that event (original["events"][:index]). A batch that removes an earlier note and revises a later edit using the ID shown at that point now binds to the intended object instead of conflicting or hitting another object.

provisional_claims.summary: Nursery: a hydrated day improved vigor only for batches still "growing"; ready batches that were kept watered gained nothing, contradicting "Hydrated days develop the batch and improve its vigor" (ready batches still need watering). Hydrated days now add vigor (+3, capped at 100) for every living batch; dry days still halt development and weaken it.
